Jane — thanks for sending this over and for the clear milestone breakdown. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Laura (finance) to align on redlines and invoicing mechanics. High-level responses while they review: 

- Milestone invoices: we can accommodate a 3-way split as long as the milestones map to deliverables in the Order Form (execution/pilot/launch). Finance will want a brief statement in the SOW or Order Form that defines the pilot completion criteria for invoicing.
- Net terms: our standard hosted offering typically sits at Net 45 for new enterprise customers; Net 60 is doable for a committed annual purchase but may require a revenue-commitment clause (minimum seasonal commit). Karthik / Laura — can you flag the tradeoffs here?
- Taxes: if GreenWave will be billed to a UK-registered entity, please provide the VAT ID and billing legal name. We will issue invoices gross; if VAT reverse-charge applies, we can reflect that with the supplied VAT ID. Laura, please confirm whether we need a W-9 or any US withholding forms for GreenWave.

If helpful, Karthik has prepared a redline with alternative language on minimum commits and invoicing cadence — I've attached it (Redwood_OrderForm_GW_v3_redline.pdf). Once we have agreement on terms, we can send for signature (DocuSign link to follow).

Jane / Irene — quick legal note after reviewing the draft and proposed split: 

1) Minimum commit: GreenWave is requesting open payment terms for the pilot. To approve Net 60 without a long-term commit, we need an express clause that either (a) ties Net 60 to an annual committed spend (we can document a minimum annual USD commit) or (b) includes a small setup fee payable on execution that is non-refundable. Our preference is option (b) for this first contract to avoid collection risk. Suggested text: 

"A non-refundable implementation fee of USD 25,000 is due on execution. Following execution, Net 45 payment terms apply unless the Customer commits to an Annual Minimum Commitment as set forth in the Order Form."

2) Milestone invoicing: Redwood can issue invoices split 50/25/25. For clarity we added a short milestone schedule in the Order Form and defined pilot completion as "successful completion of pilot test cases listed in Appendix A or written acceptance by Customer." Please confirm Appendix A scope.

3) Taxes & cross-border: If billing to the UK entity, provide VAT registration number and legal name. Redwood will invoice gross and will not withhold US taxes if Customer is not subject to US withholding. If Customer requests Redwood to assume withholding obligations, that will require revising Section X (Taxes) and could change pricing.

I've attached a redlined PDF with the above changes for quick review. If GreenWave signs off on the implementation fee approach, we can accept Net 60 only upon execution + setup fee; otherwise standard Net 45 applies.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
